To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dynamics following photoionization of BaAr clusters is governed by a sequence of electronic transitions between different electronic potential energy surfaces, and that the emission spectrum of these clusters can be understood in terms of a model based on this dynamics.

the spectroscopy of Ba(Ar) _{n} clusters is dominated by the dynamics of the excited Ba atoms, that the emission spectra are dominated by transitions from the excited Ba atom to the ground state of the Ar atoms in the cluster and by transitions from the ground state of Ba to the first excited state of the Ar cluster, and that the polarization of the emitted light is determined by the orientation of the Ba atom with respect to the Ar atoms.

we developed a theoretical model that is able to reproduce experimental spectra and polarization measurements of excited Ba(Ar) clusters, and that we used this model to obtain a complete picture of the excited cluster dynamics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spectroscopy and dynamics of electronically excited clusters, in particular of the Ba‐Ar system.
the study of the dynamics and structure of electronically excited metal‐atom clusters, using a variety of theoretical and experimental methods.
the spectroscopy and the dynamics of electronically excited rare‐gas clusters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dynamics following the photoexcitation of Ba(Ar) _{n} clusters is well understood.
the dynamics of excited Ba(Ar) _{n} is dominated by the coupling between the excited Ba atom and its nearest neighbors in the cluster.
the dynamics of the coupled nuclear‐electronic motions in the cluster can be well described by a nonadiabatic molecular‐dynamics approach using a surface‐hoppping scheme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to show that the dynamics in electronically excited Ba(Arn) clusters is dominated by transitions between different potential energy surfaces.
the dynamics of the electronically excited Ba(A)125 cluster can be described as follows: Upon excitation, energy rapidly flows from the Ba atom to the Ar atoms.
we have been able to explain spectroscopy and polarization measurements of electronically excited clusters by using a surface hopping approach for nonadiabatic molecular dynamics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use spectroscopy and molecular dynamics simulations to understand the dynamics of electronically excited clusters.
we can use the polarization of the light emitted from the clusters to gain insight into the dynamics of excited Ba(Ar) clusters.
the excited‐state dynamics of the Ba(Arn) clusters are very rich and involve many different types of processes.
